Chapter 8: Reclaiming Joy and Pleasure.
For so many of us, our bodies have felt like a source of pain, maybe even shame or fear. The idea of actually finding joy—or pleasure—in our own skin? It can seem almost impossible, maybe even a little risky. But radical self-love opens up a whole new way of seeing things. What if your body isn’t just a battleground, but a place where delight is possible?
Picture this: after years of hiding, someone finally lets themselves dance. Alone in their living room, music turned up, they move however they want—no worrying about how they look, just feeling the moment. For the first time in ages, they feel free. It’s simple, but it’s powerful. That joy? It’s proof that pleasure isn’t just for a lucky few.
Most of us have been taught to mistrust our bodies, to think pleasure is something you have to earn or strictly control. There are so many rules out there about who’s allowed to feel good, and when. But here’s the thing—those rules aren’t natural. We learn them. Radical self-love is about questioning those rules, about taking back your right to feel joy.
And pleasure? It’s not just about sex, food, or comfort. It’s in the warmth of sunlight on your skin. The taste of your favorite meal. The sound of real laughter. It’s those moments—sometimes just a second—when you actually feel at home in your body. These moments matter more than we realize. They’re tiny acts of resistance in a world that profits from making us uncomfortable.
Let me share a story. There’s a parent who’s spent years dieting, always saying no to dessert. But one birthday, they decide to eat cake with their child. The first bite, honestly, is a little awkward—there’s guilt hovering there. But then, seeing their kid’s face light up, something shifts. That pleasure? It spreads. It’s a reminder that joy is meant to be shared, not rationed.
Of course, reclaiming pleasure isn’t always easy. Old fears can sneak back in, and the world’s messages are hard to escape. But every single time you choose joy—no matter how small—you make more room for yourself. Over time, all those little moments add up. Before you know it, your life feels fuller, richer, more alive.
Radical self-love isn’t just about getting by—it’s about thriving. It’s about letting in pleasure, laughter, celebration. It’s about remembering: your body doesn’t need to apologize for existing. In fact, it’s a source of wonder.
This journey never really ends. There’ll be days when joy seems far away. But even then, the possibility is still there. No matter what, your body—with all its ups and downs—is worthy of delight.
